steps: Picked Ceasefire or Collapse from the title globe, opened What is going on here
Chose I know this on the familiarity question
Played 12 months as Ukraine mostly following cabinet picks, proposed ceasefire to Russia in month 2 (failed at 12%), signed the ceasefire in month 12
Went through the full end sequence: verdict B, 2 stars, 629/1000, achievements, moments, how you were seen, the truth, ranking
scenarios.notes: The world reacted plausibly (Trump minerals-style deal, Enerhodar plant, mobilisation age, coalition of the willing). Russia reaction text and some quotes felt generic.

steps: Used How much? and the Forecast chance to see what choices do before taking them
Read The truth screen comparing my world with the real world as of Nov 2026
scenarios.notes: Mostly yes: sizes and chances are visible, the real-world comparison at the end is exactly what I wanted. The briefing on the title screen already gave the real timeline.

friction.where: Month 1 crisis desk, cabinet pick vs mission warning
friction.expected: The pick the game labels Best trade-off to be coherent with the warning
friction.happened: Card 3 Reject it and strike was labelled Best trade-off while the cabinet pick Only by referendum was flagged as working against the mission, and card 3 itself hurts Washington. Two contradicting labels on one screen.

friction.expected: My two seals to be mine to spend
friction.happened: Staff had pre-added Reform program and National address orders that locked seals; I only noticed in the small text and had to remove them (X) to afford Propose ceasefire.

friction.where: Month 7 to 10 desk, advisor quote strip
friction.expected: Readable advisor quote and pick button
friction.happened: The quote is squeezed into a one-word-wide column and the Cabinet pick button overlaps it (Defense Minister month 7, Finance Minister month 10).

friction.expected: Orders that make sense for Ukraine
friction.happened: Staff repeatedly suggested Court Belarus (and Court UK), which no Ukrainian foreign ministry would do in this war.

friction.expected: A negative number labelled as a setback
friction.happened: United States view of you -9 sat under the label A STEP FORWARD in green.

friction.expected: Quotes that match speaker and event
friction.happened: President Donald Trump is credited with a line about the foreign ministry calling it a constructive signal, reused identically in months 3 and 9; Crowds outside the Ukrainian embassy was credited to Trump too.

friction.expected: Macron, president of France until spring 2027
friction.happened: A President Philippe Rousseau appears without any explanation of a French election.

friction.where: Title: familiarity prompt and Some help default
friction.happened: I know this was clear, hid the underlines, and I could still open the briefing. The question was fine and not noisy. Terms I did not need explained: Kramatorsk, fortress belt, coalition of the willing (all known to me); I did not need help.

friction.where: End screen The truth, Russia nuclear program card
friction.expected: Russia has an arsenal, not a program percentage
friction.happened: Russia's nuclear program 100% with strikethrough estimate and Russian strength 1221k with no unit.

friction.where: End sequence How you were seen
friction.expected: Russian state TV to claim victory
friction.happened: Russia's State Television says they blinked first, which Russian state media would never say.

friction.expected: Debrief to say what the ceasefire terms were
friction.happened: Month 12 card and newspaper say the guns fall silent but not on what terms, nothing about the annexed fifth.

bugs.title: Advisor quote column collapses and overlaps the pick button
steps: Open the desk with a crisis where the advisor quote is long
bugs.expected: Quote wraps normally in the row
bugs.actual: One word per line, pick pill drawn over the text

bugs.title: Negative result labelled A STEP FORWARD
steps: Month 1 choose Only by referendum, Execute
bugs.actual: A step forward in green with -9

bugs.title: Recycled and misattributed quotes
bugs.actual: Same Trump foreign-ministry quote on two different decisions

bugs.title: Share card text clipped
steps: End screen Ranking, scroll to share card
bugs.actual: Better than 10% of simulated leaders cut off at the right edge

bugs.title: Percentile contradicts ladder
bugs.expected: A score under the competent median not praised
bugs.actual: Headline Better than 10% of competent leaders while 629 is below median 659 and the ladder says top 10% is 717

suggestions.what: Let staff suggestions be fully off by default, or show seats they hold as a plain line next to the capital counter
Keep the real-world timeline in What is going on here and the The truth table, and add the actual ceasefire terms to the month 12 debrief
Make suggested orders country-aware: no Court Belarus for Ukraine
Match the speaker to each quote and do not reuse the same line

delight: The Ceasefire or Collapse briefing with Who is who, Why it matters and What really happened timeline up to 11 Nov 2026 (shots/priya-flash/003-about.png)
Orders refused with a reason plus a redirect (Court Russia -> Propose ceasefire instead) and a stated 12% chance (018-pc3.png)
The Enerhodar nuclear plant crisis and the mobilisation age crisis felt like the real debates
The Truth screen comparing the game world with the real world (053-end-truth.png)
The countries picker with relation labels (017-pc2.png)

fun.reason: Crises are well chosen and I was pulled along; the middle months were mostly Approve and Execute.

clarity.reason: Costs, chances and why-not messages are clear; conflicting Best trade-off versus mission warning labels and hidden staff seals hurt.

visual.reason: Polished scenes and screens, but the squashed advisor quote layout looks broken.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Strong reveal sequence and stamps; the Approve all flow feels like managing a queue.

agency.reason: I was never blocked without a reason, and refusals suggest the alternative.

realism.reason: Leaders, Enerhodar, Abu Dhabi talks and the minerals-type deal are right; Court Belarus, Russian state TV saying they blinked, a new French president and recycled quotes are wrong.

replay.reason: I want to try Russia and the US sides and to see whether refusing the referendum changes the war.

recommend.reason: I would send this to the Model UN group for the briefing and the truth screen, with a warning about the quote bugs.

verbatim: The truth screen is what I wanted from the start, my world next to what actually happened, but would a Russian paper really say they blinked?
